scope_note: Candidates are present-day photographs of surviving archaeological remains. They can inform visual texture and visible monument fragments only; they do not document Thessalonica as it looked in 380, prove the monuments' full original forms, or identify/certify an imperial headquarters site. The precise imperial seat remains uncertified.

candidates.title: Arch of Galerius, Thessaloniki
candidates.depicted_subject: Surviving brick and stone portions of the arch, sculpted pier, fenced archaeological monument, paved modern street, cars and contemporary apartment buildings.

candidates.visual_review: Downloaded original inspected at actual image level. Monument is partial/surviving fabric with modern fencing, paving, vehicles and buildings; useful for surviving masonry and sculptural relief cues, not as a complete-period reconstruction.
historical_limitations: A modern photograph of a monument associated with the late Roman/early 4th-century city, not visual evidence of its exact appearance in 380.
Surviving sections and present restoration/conservation state cannot establish original completeness, height, colors, or nearby urban context.
Does not locate or certify an imperial headquarters or palace.
candidates.architectVisualInspection: Actual downloaded JPEG viewed 2026-10-15; modern environment and fragmentary/restored fabric remain excluded from period reconstruction.

candidates.title: Forum Romanum Thessaloniki
candidates.depicted_subject: Excavated Roman forum remains in the foreground with modern residential buildings behind them.
candidates.author: Elke Brüser (Commons account: Federlesen)
candidates.license: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0)
candidates.attribution: Elke Brüser, ‘Forum Romanum Thessaloniki’, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Forum_Romanum_Thessaloniki.jpg. No changes made.
candidates.visual_review: Downloaded original inspected at actual image level. Broad modern excavation view shows low remains, arches/brickwork and contemporary apartment blocks; useful to understand the present archaeological footprint and fragmentary state.
historical_limitations: Modern excavation photograph; it does not show the forum as it appeared in 380.
Visible remains reflect excavation, later alterations and conservation; do not infer a complete ancient plan or phase from this image alone.
Modern apartment buildings dominate the background and are not period scenery.
The forum does not establish an imperial headquarters location.
